slides.narration: Two ways a project starts. Approach A is client-led — they hand you the stack, the UI preferences, the standards. Approach B is builder-led — they're vague, so you analyze and propose. Different on-ramps, same destination: a governed build.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun

slides.title: Approach A · The Client Knows What They Want

slides.title: OGE — Observability · Guardrails · Evaluation
slides.subtitle: Speed with enterprise-grade assurance

analogy.title: The three-legged stool
analogy.text: Take away any one leg and the whole thing tips. Observability without Guardrails = transparent chaos. Guardrails without Evaluation = nice fences, no inspection. Evaluation without Observability = blind testing. All three or nothing.

list.name: Observability
list.desc: Traceability and transparency by design — every AI prompt, every code commit, every business event LOGGED. No black-boxes.

list.name: Guardrails
list.desc: Policies + templates + technical controls that BOUND how AI may act — from prompt structure to CI/CD deployment gates.

list.name: Evaluation
list.desc: Continuous multi-layer quality + risk checks — functional, security, performance, AI output, regression. Not a late QA phase.

slides.memory_hook: O = SEE what happened. G = SET what's allowed. E = CHECK that quality held.
slides.closing_thread: Let's zoom into each pillar — starting with the one that catches issues BEFORE they become incidents.
slides.narration: OGE — Observability, Guardrails, Evaluation. Three pillars. A three-legged stool. Take any one away and the whole thing tips. Observability is seeing what happened. Guardrails is what's allowed. Evaluation is verifying quality held.

slides.title: Observability — See Everything
slides.subtitle: Pillar 1 of 3 · Full transparency by design

analogy.title: Black box vs. flight recorder
analogy.text: Planes don't fly without flight recorders. Every input, every output, every decision is logged. When something goes wrong — and it will — you don't guess. You replay.

list.name: AI Interaction Logging
list.desc: Every prompt + every AI response logged. Complete audit trail of HOW the code came to exist.

list.name: Code Versioning
list.desc: Every AI-generated commit goes into Git. Full history, rollback, ownership clarity.

list.name: System Monitoring
list.desc: API logs, error tracking, performance metrics in real time.

list.name: Business Event Tracking
list.desc: Workflow-level logging — approvals, validations, status transitions. Business rules made visible.

slides.memory_hook: No black-box behaviour. Every decision and output is fully explainable.
slides.reflection_prompt: Think of a system you've used at work. If something went wrong, could anyone tell you EXACTLY what happened and why? If no — that's an observability gap.
slides.closing_thread: Next: the fences that bound AI's behaviour.
slides.narration: Observability. Four areas. AI interaction logging — every prompt and response stored. Code versioning — every commit in Git. System monitoring — real-time metrics. Business event tracking — workflow-level transparency. No black boxes anywhere.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Observability is the flight recorder of your app. Planes don't fly without one.

slides.title: Guardrails — Set What's Allowed
slides.subtitle: Pillar 2 of 3 · Enterprise control mechanisms

analogy.title: Highway guardrails, not free-fall
analogy.text: Roads have rails not because drivers are bad, but because at speed you don't get a second chance. Same with AI: at 100x speed, you don't get a do-over on a security breach.

list.name: Prompt Guardrails
list.desc: Structured requirement templates. Mandatory business rules + edge cases. Reduces ambiguous or unsafe AI outputs.

list.name: Code Guardrails
list.desc: OWASP-aligned secure coding. Mandatory input validation + error handling. No deployment of unreviewed AI code.

list.name: Access Control
list.desc: RBAC. Least-privilege principle. Server-side authorization on EVERY request — never just UI.

list.name: Data Protection
list.desc: No sensitive data in prompts. Masking/tokenisation when required. GDPR / SOC 2 / ISO 27001 alignment.

list.name: Deployment Guardrails
list.desc: Mandatory approval checkpoints. Security validation + test-pass criteria. Controlled CI/CD pipelines.

slides.memory_hook: Five fences: Prompt · Code · Access · Data · Deployment. Skip any one = production fire.
slides.closing_thread: And finally: how we PROVE quality held — that's Evaluation.
slides.narration: Guardrails. Five categories. Prompt guardrails — structured templates. Code guardrails — OWASP-aligned with no unreviewed deployment. Access control — RBAC with server-side enforcement. Data protection — no sensitive data in prompts, GDPR-aligned. Deployment guardrails — controlled CI/CD with approval checkpoints.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: Guardrails. Highway rails, not free-fall. At AI speed you don't get a do-over on a breach.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: Five categories. PROMPT guardrails — your prompt templates have mandatory fields. Business rules, edge cases, security expectations.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: CODE guardrails — OWASP top ten baked in. Every input validated. No unreviewed AI code ships to production. Ever.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: ACCESS CONTROL — role-based, least-privilege, and server-side enforced. Not just UI-hidden. Real backend checks on every single request.

narration_script.speaker: Sara
narration_script.text: DATA PROTECTION — never paste customer PII into your prompts. Mask, tokenize, GDPR-align. Treat AI tools as you treat any third-party.

narration_script.speaker: Arjun
narration_script.text: DEPLOYMENT — controlled pipelines, approval gates, security scans before promote. The CI/CD is itself a guardrail.

slides.title: Evaluation — Check Quality Held
slides.subtitle: Pillar 3 of 3 · Continuous quality assurance

analogy.title: Continuous QA vs. end-of-line inspector
analogy.text: An end-of-line inspector catches the bad pizza after it's plated. Continuous QA catches the bad ingredient before it ever hits the oven. OrchestrAI ships the second style — by design.

list.name: Functional
list.desc: Business requirement accuracy. Test cases mapped one-to-one with requirements.

list.name: Security
list.desc: SAST scans. Dependency vulnerability checks. Auth + access tests per route.

list.name: Performance
list.desc: Load testing. Response time benchmarks. Scalability validation.

list.name: AI Output
list.desc: Accuracy of generated logic. Edge-case validation. Hallucination checks.

list.name: Regression
list.desc: Automated suites on every meaningful update. Stability across changes.

slides.memory_hook: Five layers: Functional · Security · Performance · AI Output · Regression. Continuous, not late-stage.
slides.closing_thread: Three pillars covered. Now: the 10 non-negotiable practices that operationalize OGE.
slides.narration: Evaluation. Five layers. Functional — business requirements verified one-to-one. Security — SAST and dependency scans. Performance — load testing and benchmarks. AI Output — hallucination and edge-case checks. Regression — automated suites on every update.

narration_script.speaker: Sara

slides.title: Spot the OGE gaps in this opening prompt
slides.subtitle: Click on every part that breaks governance discipline
slides.text: Build me a project tracker app fast. Use whatever stack you think is best. Skip the docs and just generate the code so we can demo it tomorrow. We will add tests later.

flaws.phrase: whatever stack you think is best
flaws.explanation: No stack pinned = no consistency. T1 demands the stack be in the attached kit BEFORE the AI generates code. Otherwise every regenerate produces a different framework.
Documents ARE the governance. Skipping them means no FDD, no TDD, no DB design. The AI has nothing to constrain it. Drift is guaranteed.
Evaluation is continuous, not late-stage. 'Tests later' = the third OGE pillar isn't operational. By the time you add tests, bugs are in production.
